decisions.reason: Correctly walks resolve(): snapshot no longer has `current`, id is undefined every keystroke, null return exits onKeyDown before preventDefault; explains guard passing (all four presence probes still truthy) and the silent no-op (undefined read + deliberate early return), without claiming removal/throw of the sessions service or guard.

Walks both session-list type excerpts showing current removed and navigation moved to view owners, then grounds the canonical replacement in the ui-session excerpt: uiSession.adapter.current yielding SessionBindingValue with key replacing current and ctx replacing sessions.scope(id); notes mapping to the change without relying on it.

Proposes a corrected resolve() that feature-detects uiSession and reads adapter.current.getSnapshot() (key for id, binding.ctx.get('conversation'), input.for(binding.ctx)) with a legacy fallback branch reading current plus sessions.scope(id); inject gains uiSession (optional), one build for both hosts; no slot re-registration or removed-field read on the new path.

Names the class (field-level removal behind stable service-level presence, checked once at activation while breakage recurs per use) and specifies probing the actual capability — asserting the snapshot field on legacy-shaped hosts and feature-detecting/asserting uiSession's key/ctx on alpha.2 — with a lazy first-use materialization probe, noting presence-list expansion alone is insufficient.

Covers dual-host behavioral verification with chord checks (including the swallow-vs-cursor symptom) and a live probe of adapter.current key/ctx via inspect tooling, plus a strong prevention design (throwing/deprecated getter on read). But it never proposes typechecking against the published alpha.2 types as the pre-ship gate, and its prevention rationale even downplays type-only gates.
